The Skellam distribution models the difference between two independent Poisson variables, which is essential for computing spread cover probabilities in soccer/hockey/baseball. The system uses λ (rate parameter) derived from TeamGameLog to compute these probabilities, renormalizing for pushes. This enables a new ranking layer that treats spread outcomes independently from moneyline outcomes. The `skellam_cover` primitive computes 2-way cover probabilities, which are then used exclusively by `scoreSpreadPick` to derive rankings. Moneyline rankings remain unaffected, preserving their independence. The system ensures that only valid sports (Poisson-compatible) use this mechanism, excluding NFL due to its unique Stern key-number dynamics. This creates a dualistic framework where spread and moneyline rankings operate under different probabilistic assumptions, enhancing model calibration and interpretability.
